decisions.reason: Because it extends the firm's core wafer and packaging capabilities, management is likely to continue it rather than write off related development work and admit a mistake on a technically adjacent product.

As a close, practical extension of the established carrier-wafer business, it likely required limited new capabilities and gives management little reason to retreat while industry demand is still favorable.
Since it was presented as a flagship and launched publicly at SEMICON Europa, the firm's visible commitment and likely R&D investment make escalation of commitment especially strong.
Because the firm created a dedicated brand and framed it as part of its strategic direction, dropping it would be a very public reversal that management is strongly inclined to avoid.

As the most distant product from the firm's established substrate business and without the same level of public strategic commitment as C or D, it is the easiest offering for management to cut and reallocate resources away from.
